required_cases.required_result: Unrelated work updates succeed without semantic conflicts or another stream's context/denominator changing.
Only one valid writer owns a work; changing work branches cannot evade the guard.
Separate worktrees can edit their files independently; shared external and integration resources still conflict.
Old fences and epochs cannot update current ownership or dispatch new effects.
Identical requests replay receipts, unknown effects retain reservations, duplicate usage receipts are not double charged.
A cyclic union cannot commit even when concurrent graph edits are individually acyclic; cross-stream task DAGs remain usable.
Revocation after preparation blocks affected dispatch/completion without erasing history.
A valid pinned delivery survives unrelated newer work; explicit revocation requires reassessment.
Search/count/event/artifact/recovery/cache paths cannot leak unauthorized stream state; permitted dependency exports remain usable.
Concurrent sources and interrupted activation cannot lose updates or expose a mixed authoritative snapshot.
Shared work counts once, planning does not change contract denominators, unknown usage stays unknown and parallel time is not summed wall time.
Administrative barriers hold across concurrent writers and legacy clients retain compatible behavior or receive an explicit refusal.

performance.latency_and_tokens: Compare the same workload and facts against the recorded pre-change binary. Report distribution, database serialization and absent measurements. A domain benchmark alone cannot establish native-client cost or latency.
